merger_description:
ACURIO Health Pty Ltd (**Acurio**) proposes to acquire three private hospitals located in the greater Sydney area from Healthscope Operations Pty Ltd (**Healthscope**) (the **Acquisition**). The three private hospitals that are the subject of the Acquisition are:

* Nepean Private Hospital in Kingswood;
* Sydney Southwest Private Hospital in Liverpool; and
* Campbelltown Private Hospital in Campbelltown.

The Acquisition forms part of a broader consortium acquisition of Healthscope's portfolio. The other consortium members are Calvary, Healthe Care and KnG Group, which will each acquire separate hospitals pursuant to inter-conditional sale agreements.

Acurio is a private hospital operator, which currently operates The George Centre in the Gledswood Hills and Sydney Day Hospital in the Sydney central business district. The George Centre is a 61-bed private hospital offering overnight accommodation. It offers maternity and paediatric services, with a 26-bed private maternity unit, as well as a range of other surgical services. Sydney Day Hospital is a day surgery which does not offer overnight accommodation.

Healthscope operates a network of private hospitals across Australia. On 26 May 2025, Healthscope's parent entities entered into receivership, with McGrathNicol appointed as Receivers to complete a sale of the business. The Receivers conducted an extended sale process over Healthscope's hospital portfolio.

events.title: Acurio - Nepean, Sydney Southwest, and Campbelltown Private Hospitals - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details: The reasons for the ACCC’s determination are set out in section 2.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines.

In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered the information and documents that were submitted with the notification form, additional information provided by the parties to the Acquisition, information provided by third parties and market feedback.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect.
Background on voluntary administration of Healthscope and consortium acquisition

In May 2025, Healthscope’s parent entities went into voluntary administration, and receivers (Receivers) and administrators were appointed by its lenders and the Healthscope Board respectively to conduct an orderly sale of the hospitals in its network. The Receivers conducted an extended sale process over Healthscope's hospital portfolio.

The Acquisition forms part of a broader consortium acquisition of Healthscope's portfolio, following the Receivers’ sale process. The other members of the consortium are Calvary, Healthe Care and KnG Group, which each propose to acquire separate hospitals pursuant to inter-conditional sale agreements.
Acurio (through The George Centre) overlaps with Sydney Southwest Private and Campbelltown Private in the supply of private hospital services in south-west Sydney and surrounding areas, specifically:

items.text: the supply of medical, surgical and emergency care services across a range of medical specialties to patients;
the supply of private hospital facilities, equipment and support staff to visiting medical officers (VMOs); and
the supply of Hospital Purchaser Provider Agreements to private health insurers.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC considers there is no material overlap between Acurio’s existing hospitals and Nepean Private Hospital.

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed.

The ACCC has considered whether the Acquisition is likely to substantially lessen competition in the supply of private hospital services to patients, VMOs or private health insurers in south-west Sydney and surrounding areas.

For the purpose of its assessment, it was not necessary to reach a definitive view on the precise product or geographic boundaries of the relevant market, as it does not materially alter the ACCC’s competition assessment.

The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the supply of private hospital services to patients, VMOs or private health insurers in south-west Sydney and surrounding areas.
Based on information provided by the Parties and by third parties, the ACCC makes the following findings:

items.text: The George Centre, Sydney Southwest Private and Campbelltown Private have overlapping geographical catchment zones for patients, with each attracting patients largely from south-west Sydney and surrounding areas.
However, there is no real commercial likelihood of an alternative purchaser acquiring the Target Hospitals.

In the absence of a commercially realistic alternative purchaser, and in the context of Healthscope’s voluntary administration, there is not a real prospect that the Target Hospitals would continue operating as private hospitals in the future without the Acquisition.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC considers that, while the Acquisition would reduce the number of independent suppliers of private hospital services in south-west Sydney and surrounding areas, a reduction would also occur absent the Acquisition. Accordingly, the Acquisition is unlikely to result in a substantial lessening of competition relative to the future without the Acquisition.
